info.title: Inbils Mobile API
info.description:
Contract of the Inbils customer and technician mobile apps. The apps hand-write their models from this document.
Regenerate it with `php artisan scramble:export` after any change to an `api/v1` route, request or resource.

## Authentication

Every endpoint except `POST auth/login`, `POST auth/two-factor` and `POST auth/forgot-password` needs
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A token belongs to one app install and carries one ability, `customer` or
`technician`, picked by the `app` field at login. A token expires 90 days (customer) or 30 days (technician) after it
is issued. `POST auth/token/refresh` swaps it for a new one; refresh when fewer than 7 days remain. Any 401 means
"sign in again". Logout, a password change, deactivation, a 2FA change and `DELETE devices/{id}` revoke tokens.

A user with confirmed two-factor authentication gets `202` from `POST auth/login` with a `challenge_id` (valid 300 s,
5 attempts) and no token. `POST auth/two-factor` with a TOTP or recovery code then issues the token.

## Errors

Every error under `api/v1` is JSON: `{"message": string, "code": string, "errors"?: {field: [string]}, "request_id": string}`.
`message` is for developers and may be English or Indonesian; show your own text per `code`. `errors` appears only
with `validation_failed`. `request_id` equals the `X-Request-Id` response header: quote it when you report a problem,
and the server log can be searched by it. A 429 carries `Retry-After` (seconds).

| Status | `code` |
|---|---|
| 400 | `bad_request` |
| 401 | `unauthenticated` (missing, expired or revoked token), `account_inactive` (the token is deleted) |
| 403 | `forbidden` (wrong app ability or no permission), `app_not_allowed` (the account may not use this app), `password_reset_required` |
| 404 | `not_found` (also another customer's or company's record), `payment_unavailable` (online payment is off) |
| 405 | `method_not_allowed` |
| 408 | `request_timeout` |
| 409 | `conflict`, `idempotency_in_progress`, `push_token_not_registered` (this install's push token is not registered for this sign-in) |
| 413 | `payload_too_large` |
| 415 | `unsupported_media_type` |
| 422 | `validation_failed`, `unprocessable` (a well-formed request the business rules refuse), `idempotency_conflict`, `invoice_not_payable`, `challenge_expired` |
| 428 | `precondition_required`, `idempotency_key_required` |
| 429 | `too_many_requests` |
| 500 | `server_error` |
| 503 | `push_unavailable` (push notifications are off on the server) |
| other 4xx | `client_error` |

## Idempotency

Every `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` except the three public auth endpoints needs `Idempotency-Key: <UUID>`
(missing: 428 `idempotency_key_required`; not a UUID: 422 `validation_failed`). Generate one key per user action and
reuse it for every retry of that action. For 24 hours the server stores the response per user and key:

- a retry with the same request gets the stored status and body again, with the header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`;
- the same key with a different request is 422 `idempotency_conflict`;
- the same key while the first request still runs is 409 `idempotency_in_progress`;
- 5xx and 429 responses are not stored, so retry them with the same key.

## Identifiers

Every `id` and every field that names another record (`customer_id`, `subscription_id`, ...) is an opaque string: a
26-character lowercase ULID such as `01m5441c2q1sqrw67nr4dwyakz`. Keep it as a string, never parse or order it as a
number, and send it back unchanged in paths and bodies. Version 1.1 replaced the integer ids of 1.0. An integer or
unknown id in a path answers 404 `not_found`; in a body it is 422 `validation_failed`. A notification's `id` is a UUID.

## Pagination

List endpoints answer `{data, links, meta}` (Laravel paginator). `?page=` starts at 1. `?per_page=` defaults to 20,
at most 50. One record is `{data}`.

## Rate limits

120 requests a minute per token, 20 sign-ins a minute per IP, 6 password-reset requests a minute per IP, 6 payment
starts, 30 uploads and 30 promo banner taps a minute per user, 3 push tests a minute per user.

post.summary:
A user with a confirmed second factor gets a challenge and nothing else: what the account may do in the
app is only checked once the code passed, so a password alone reveals nothing about it

The answer never depends on the address, and the link goes out after the response, so neither the body
nor the time it takes says whether an account exists (as on the web)

post.description:
Send it after sign-in and whenever Firebase hands the app a new one. A token the server already knows is moved to
this user and this sign-in (200), a new one is stored (201). Logging out, a revoked sign-in or an expired one
ends pushes to the install, so register again after the next login.

delete.description: Always 204: a token that is unknown, or that belongs to another user, is left alone and not revealed.

post.description:
Writes a `push_test` notification in the bell and pushes it to the install that holds `token`, never to the user's
other phones. 202: the push is queued, the app waits `wait_seconds` for it. 409 `push_token_not_registered`: the
server does not know this token for this sign-in (register it with `POST me/device-token` and retry), 503
`push_unavailable`: push is off on the server. At most 3 a minute per user.
post.summary: Send a test push to this install

get.description:
Read live from RADIUS. `data` is null while there is nothing true to say: RADIUS is switched off or
unreachable, or the subscription has no PPPoE account. `online` carries `since` (when the session started),
`offline` carries `last_seen_at` (when the last session ended, null if none has); both are ISO 8601 with an
offset. Only the status and those two times leave the server, never an address or a session id.
get.summary: Whether the PPPoE line of the subscription is up now

post.description: Only while the SPK is assigned, and only once: asking again changes nothing and returns the SPK as it is. The status stays `assigned`; the SPK moves to the `en_route` step and the customer's app is told. The location fix is optional and kept apart from the check-in of the start.
post.summary: Tell the customer the technician has left for the visit

delete.description: A line the manager planned (a reservation or a note) stays with `quantity_used` 0; a line that held nothing but this use is deleted. The answer is 204 either way, so read the SPK again to see which. A serialized asset line is refused with 422.
delete.summary: Withdraw the technician's use of a product

post.description: Only for the technician the SPK is assigned to now, and only while it is assigned or in progress; a reassignment ends the access. Every call is audited and counts against 5 a minute. The answer is never cached or kept for an `Idempotency-Key` replay: ask again to see it again. 409 `work_order_closed` when the SPK is no longer active, 422 `credentials_not_ready` when the account is not made yet.
post.summary: Show the PPPoE login of an installation SPK

ChangePasswordRequest.description:
Changing the password from the app. The current password is the only step-up a bearer token has, so a stolen
token must not be a free place to guess it: wrong guesses are limited per user and address with the key and
budget of the web's confirm-password step (ConfirmablePasswordController), counted before the password is
checked. The check is therefore not a validation rule: rules run before the controller can claim an attempt.
ChangePasswordRequest.title: ChangePasswordRequest

reference.description: The gateway order id for an online payment; null for a manual one, whose staff-typed reference stays internal.

suspension_reason.description:
Why a suspended subscription is on hold; null for any other status. `overdue` lifts by itself once the unpaid
bills are paid, `manual` waits for the ISP. A suspension recorded before the reason existed is null too.

reactivation_holds.description:
The unpaid bills a subscription isolated for overdue bills still waits for: it is reconnected by itself once none
is left, so the customer pays all of them. Oldest due first; empty in every other state, and when the ISP
reconnects by hand.

speed_label.description: Marketing speed, e.g. "Hingga 50 Mbps": the maximum download of the speed profile.

sla_tier.description: The service level the package was sold with.

pppoe_username.description: The PPPoE login the customer types into the router. Never the password.

handler_first_name.description: First name of the staff member handling the ticket; null while unassigned. The rest of the profile stays internal.

can_reply.description: False once the ticket is closed: replies are refused and the customer is pointed to a new ticket.

reopened_at.description: When a reply of the customer last brought the resolved ticket back; null if it never did.

state.description:
`open` while the visit is under way (also while the office sends work back), `done` once the technician has
finished (the office's review is not the customer's concern), `cancelled`.

steps.description:
The four steps of the visit. `current` is the last one reached: it and the steps before it are reached and only
those carry a time, which is null for a step that was skipped. Empty for a cancelled visit.

current.description: The last step reached; null when none has (and for a cancelled visit).

LoginRequest.description:
The web login's credential check, user lookup (inactive users fail like a wrong password) and failed-attempt
budget, shared with the web through the same throttle key, plus the device and the app the token is for.
Only the answer to the budget differs: the app gets a 429 with Retry-After, not a form error.
LoginRequest.title: LoginRequest

company.description: The ISP behind the login, as the apps brand themselves with it after sign-in. Every field is null until the ISP fills it in.

logo_url.description: Absolute URL of the company logo. Public: fetch it without the bearer token. An SVG logo is served as SVG.

brand_color.description: `#RRGGBB` the ISP picked on the company page; the app theme is seeded from it.

whatsapp.description: Digits and `( ) + -` only, as the ISP typed it.

type.description:
What happened. The apps pick an icon and wording from it and open `subject`; an unrecognised value is shown
with `title` and `message` as they are. `invoice_reminder` is only on rows written before `invoice_due_soon`
and `invoice_overdue` replaced it.

subscription_id.description: The subscription this invoice bills; null when it belongs to no single subscription.

customer_name.description: The customer's name as printed when the invoice was issued; a later rename does not change it.

customer_address.description: The customer's address as printed when the invoice was issued; null when the customer had none.

package_name.description: The package name as printed when the invoice was issued; null for an invoice without a subscription.

billing_period.description: The service period the invoice bills; null for an invoice without one.

reference.description: The gateway order id for an online payment; null for a manual one, whose staff-typed reference stays internal.

StoreDeviceTokenRequest.description:
An app install registers the FCM token it just got (or refreshed) for the signed-in user. The app named in the body
must be the one this bearer token was issued for: a customer token cannot register a technician install.
StoreDeviceTokenRequest.title: StoreDeviceTokenRequest

work_order_id.description:
The caller's own SPK, assigned or in progress, by its public id. The request is then the material of that SPK:
what the warehouse hands over is counted against it, so SPK approval does not take the same material again.
Omit it, or send null, for a request that belongs to no SPK.

reason.description: Left blank, the service writes its own reason.

quantity_approved.description: What the office approved (null until it did) and what the warehouse handed over, so the card shows more than the ask.

cancel.description: Own request, still waiting for the warehouse: InventoryRequestPolicy::cancel.

available.description:
What is free to ask for at the warehouse the request named (stock minus reserved, "0" when it holds none of
this product), as a decimal without trailing zeros. Null when the request named no warehouse.

handler_first_name.description: First name of the staff member handling the ticket; null while unassigned. The rest of the profile stays internal.

first_response_source.description: What counted as the first response: a public staff reply ('reply'), the Mulai button ('start') or nothing yet (null).

last_used.description: True for the warehouse of the caller's latest request: the picker of a new request starts there.

type_label.description: The type in Indonesian, as the app shows it: never show `type` itself.

steps.description:
The four steps of the visit. `current` is the last one reached: it and the steps before it are reached and only
those carry a time, which is null for a step that was skipped. Empty for a cancelled SPK.

current.description: The last step reached; null when none has (a draft, a waiting SPK, a cancelled one).

phone_e164.description: The phone as `+62…` for a WhatsApp link (`https://wa.me/` without the plus); null when it is not an Indonesian mobile number.

network_account.description:
The PPPoE login of an installation, for the technician it is assigned to: the username and where it stands,
never the secret (the app asks for that behind "Tampilkan", POST network-credentials). Null for any other
type, while no account is made, and for anyone but the assignee.

site.description: Where to go: the customer's installation address for a subscription SPK, else the SPK's location.

pop.description: The POP the SPK is stocked from, apart from the site; null when the site is the location itself.

en_route.description: "Berangkat" is offered once: after it the next action is the start.

edit_items.description: Whoever may submit the SPK (its assigned technician, while it is in progress) keeps its material lines.

customer_hint.description: A short tip the ISP wrote for this category ("Saran untuk pelanggan"), at most 500 characters; null when it wrote none.

TwoFactorRequest.description:
Step two of an app login: the challenge from the password step and one code (TOTP or recovery code).

The brute-force budgets are those of the web challenge, TwoFactorChallengeRequest, and use the same
limiter keys, so wrong codes sent from the app and from the browser add up. The web request keeps its
limits private; they are repeated here and pinned by tests/Feature/Api/V1/Auth/TwoFactorLoginTest.
TwoFactorRequest.title: TwoFactorRequest

phone.description: The web's customer rule, plus the space people type inside a number; null clears it.

errors.description: A detailed description of each field that failed validation.

code.description: Stable error code; see the API description.

request_id.description: Equals the X-Request-Id response header; quote it when reporting a problem.
